headline: Phillies' season over after Wild Card Series loss to Braves
recap: Two days removed from elimination, the Phillies' season ended Thursday night in Atlanta with a 6-2 loss in the decisive Game 3 of the NL Wild Card Series. Michael Harris II's three-run homer in the bottom of the first put the Braves up 3-0 off starter Aaron Nola, who was pulled after 1 2/3 innings with all three runs charged to him. Zack Wheeler relieved and allowed a two-run homer to Ozzie Albies in the fourth that made it 5-0. Philadelphia got on the board in the sixth when Alec Bohm's groundout scored Kyle Schwarber off Robert Suarez, with Bryce Harper advancing to third. Jonathan Bowlan gave up a solo homer to Matt Olson in the seventh that made it 6-1, and Trea Turner's eighth-inning sacrifice fly off Dylan Dodd, scoring Derek Hill, closed out the scoring at 6-2. Grant Holmes got the win in relief for Atlanta; Nola took the loss.

Philadelphia finished the regular season 88-74, second in the NL East, six games behind the division-winning Braves. The Phillies reached the postseason as a wild card and were eliminated 2-1 in the best-of-three Wild Card Series, falling in Game 3 after splitting the first two games, both also played in Atlanta.
There is no next game: the Phillies' season is over. Atlanta advances in the NL playoffs while Philadelphia moves into the offseason.
